title: Registry thundering CI churn -> node image-gc spike and kubelet restarts (incident notes)
content:
Summary:

Short: On 2025-02-14 ~10:40 UTC a burst of CI job starts (internal runners) caused a flood of parallel image pulls which saturated node disk bandwidth and caused aggressive kubelet image garbage collection (image-gc) activity. The image-gc loop, combined with containerd snapshot churn, triggered repeated kubelet restarts on 5 worker nodes and a scheduling backlog for ~17 minutes. API server latency spiked to ~1.2s p95 and several small services observed request timeouts.

Why this is different from recent node-pressure incidents:
- Root trigger was not long-term memory/disk leak but a short-lived high-concurrency image-pull spike from workers (CI autoscale event).
- The kubelet image-gc parameters and containerd snapshotter behavior led to a tight loop where GC work tried to reclaim disk space but concurrently new image layers were being written, producing high iowait and kernel reclaim pressure.

Detection (how it was first noticed):
- Pager alerted: "kubelet restarted" (5 nodes) at 10:45 UTC.
- Cloudwatch/Prometheus: node_disk_io_time p95 jumped; containerd_pull_duration p95 went from 0.9s -> 6.8s; kubelet_restart_count increased.
- Slack: CI job failures started appearing in #ci-notifications around 10:42 UTC.

Timeline (reconstructed):
- 10:36 UTC: Autoscaler scaled runners pool from 120 -> 420 for a timed CI spike (scheduled load).
- 10:38 UTC: Many new runner pods launched across cluster, concurrently pulling large images (~600MB average).
- 10:40 UTC: Node disk write/flush latency climbs, containerd image pull latencies rise.
- 10:41 UTC: Kubelet image-gc kicks in aggressively due to ephemeral-storage soft eviction thresholds; image-gc enters repeated prune cycles (logs show repeated calls to ensureImageStorage and removal attempts).
- 10:43 UTC: Kernel dmesg shows block layer IO latency warnings and several 'ext4: delayed allocation bug' style messages on affected nodes.
- 10:44 UTC: Kubelet crashes with OOM_kill-like stack traces in system journal on 5 nodes; systemd restarts kubelet, but restarts cause transient control-plane load.
- 10:46 UTC: API server p95 latency 1.2s, scheduler Pending pods backlog grows to ~250 pods cluster-wide (mostly small service replicas and CI job pods).
- 10:53 UTC: We cordoned the 5 affected nodes and scaled the registry replica set + caching layer; we also throttled CI job concurrency via temporary GitLab runner config change.
- 11:03 UTC: kubelet restarts subsided, image-pull latency falls back, pending backlog drains by 11:16 UTC.

Immediate mitigation steps taken (chronological):
1) 10:46 UTC - emergency: cordon the 5 worst nodes (node-54..node-58) to prevent more scheduling to flapping nodes.
2) 10:47 UTC - scaled up internal registry cache proxies (two additional pods) to reduce cross-region pulls.
3) 10:48 UTC - temporarily reduced CI runner concurrency on the autoscaling group (set max concurrent jobs to 2 per runner).
4) 10:51 UTC - applied a temporary kubelet config change via daemonset that increased image-gc high threshold from 85% -> 92% (fast patch via restart; note: this is invasive and not ideal long-term).
5) 10:57 UTC - rebalanced some running CI pods to less-loaded nodes manually (kubectl drain gracefully, migrate ephemeral workloads).
6) 11:03 UTC - uncordoned nodes after observing stable kubelet and disk metrics for 8+ minutes.

Logs / useful queries we used: (promql / journal hints)
- PromQL: increase(containerd_engine_pull_count[5m]) by (instance) to spot pull storm.
- PromQL: node_filesystem_avail_bytes / node_filesystem_size_bytes to see ephemeral-storage headroom.
- node_disk_io_time_seconds_total p95 on affected instances.
- journalctl -u kubelet -S "2025-02-14 10:30:00" | grep -E "image-gc|ensureImageStorage|eviction"
- containerd events: ctr events --namespace k8s.io --since 2025-02-14T10:30:00Z | grep -i pull

Root cause analysis (current hypothesis):
- Primary: Scheduled CI autoscaler event created a thundering herd of concurrent image pulls. The registry (primary region) handled the traffic but many layers were uncached at the node level and spread across nodes, causing heavy disk write amplification.
- Secondary: Kubelet image-gc logic and containerd snapshotter interacted poorly under this workload. Image-gc's eviction decision path triggered frequent removal attempts while new layers were being streamed to disk, leading to heavy unlink/write churn and high kernel-level IO latency. The kubelet experienced memory pressure (due to GC bookkeeping) and was OOM-killed intermittently on affected nodes.
- Contributing: No pre-pulled images for the CI runners, overly permissive CI concurrency for scheduled runs, registry cache layer had insufficient capacity for the burst, and kubelet image-gc defaults are tuned for long-term steady-state not short bursty pulls.

Post-incident action items (owner -> due):
- SRE-4521 (Ethan) - Add circuit-breaker to CI autoscaler to limit concurrent new runner launches per region (due 2025-02-21).
- SRE-4522 (Maya) - Implement node-level pre-pull DaemonSet for CI runner images during scheduled heavy runs (prototype runbook, due 2025-02-28).
- SRE-4523 (Jordan) - Harden registry cache autoscaling (increase headroom and add health-based scaling) and add usage alarms (due 2025-02-24).
- SRE-4524 (SRE team) - Update kubelet image-gc tuning guidance in cluster runbook: revisit high/low thresholds, debounce logic, and recommend safer runtime patch approach (draft changes by 2025-03-03).
- SRE-4525 (Platform-eng) - Investigate swapping snapshotter to overlaybd/nydus for heavy-pull workloads or tune containerd snapshotter GC on our AMIs (investigation due 2025-03-10).
- SRE-4526 (Sofia) - Add an alert for "image-pull-rate vs image-gc rate divergence" (detect when pulls >> deletes over 5m) (due 2025-02-20).

Runbook updates (immediate notes to add):
- New checklist for rapid response to image-pull storms: 1) confirm registry health -> 2) throttle CI autoscaler -> 3) scale registry cache -> 4) cordon most-affected nodes -> 5) avoid immediate kubelet config restarts unless confirmed benefit.
- Add playbook to pre-warm runner images before known heavy scheduled runs (cronjob that pre-pulls to nodes or a nodepool with pre-pulled images).
- Document safer kubelet GC adjustments (make changes via machine image/rolling update, not on-the-fly via daemonset except as absolute last resort).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did kubelet memory bookkeeping grow enough to trigger OOM on several nodes? Need deeper heap/profile traces around image-gc loop (Jordan to collect kubelet heap profiles next repro).
- Are there edge cases where the containerd snapshotter will deadlock under concurrent remove+write operations? Need containerd engineering to review (linked ticket).
- Should we implement admission control to limit concurrent image pulls cluster-wide? (tradeoffs to discuss with product/CI teams).

Metrics to monitor going forward (new dashboards):
- image_pull_concurrency by node (new metric derived from containerd pull start/finish).
- image_gc_cycles per node per minute and deletes_attempted vs deletes_successful ratio.
- registry cache hit rate and cross-region egress bandwidth.
- kubelet restart_count and OOM_kill events per node.

Postmortem severity classification: SEV3 (service degradation with user-visible timeouts, partial scheduling impact). Rationale: short-lived, contained to 5 nodes, control-plane latency increase, system recovery via mitigations without data loss.

Lessons learned (short):
- Short, high-concurrency workloads (CI bursts) are a different failure mode than slow drift; our operational tuning and autoscaling policies need explicit handling for burst profiles.
- Image lifecycle (pull vs gc) interactions are a recurring low-level operational risk for containerd/kubelet — we should treat it as a first-class scenario in runbooks.

Appendix (raw log snippets):
- journal excerpt (kubelet):
  Feb 14 10:44:21 node-56 kubelet[1023]: I0214 10:44:21.123456 1023 image_gc.go:375] image-gc: attempting to reclaim 322345600 bytes
  Feb 14 10:44:21 node-56 kubelet[1023]: E0214 10:44:21.234567 1023 kubelet.go:2201] runtime service error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to remove snapshot: device or resource busy
  Feb 14 10:44:45 node-56 kernel: [290341.123456] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
  Feb 14 10:44:47 node-56 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL

- containerd events sample:
  2025-02-14T10:41:03Z containerd: "pull start" image=registry.internal/redwood/ci-runner:sha-abc123
  2025-02-14T10:41:04Z containerd: "pull ok" image=... duration=4.2s
  2025-02-14T10:42:10Z containerd: "remove snapshot" id=sha-... error="device busy"

Notes for the next incident drill:
- Run a tabletop exercise simulating scheduled CI bursts and exercise the new runbook steps (owner: Sofia, target date: 2025-03-12).
- Include registry and containerd engineers in the drill to walk through mitigations that don't rely on restarting kubelet.

End of notes.
